references.text: David's psalm that prophesies about the Messiah sitting at God's right hand: "Sit at my right hand" ([ref:Ps 110:1|Psalms 110:1]). Jesus applies this prophecy to himself as the Son of Man who will sit at God's right hand – "ἐκ δεξιῶν τῆς δυνάμεως τοῦ θεοῦ".

Daniel's vision of "one like a son of man" who came before the Ancient of Days and was given dominion, glory, and a kingdom ([ref:Dan 7:13-14|Daniel 7:13-14]). Jesus uses the title "Son of Man" (ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου) from this prophecy and links it to his exaltation at God's right hand.

Matthew's parallel account of Jesus' words before the high council, where he says that they "from now on will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming on the clouds of heaven" ([ref:Matt 26:64|Matthew 26:64]). The parallel is almost word-for-word, but Luke omits the mention of coming on the clouds.

Mark's parallel account where Jesus answers the high priest: "You will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming with the clouds of heaven" ([ref:Mark 14:62|Mark 14:62]). Together with Matthew's parallel, this shows that Luke records the same statement but emphasizes "from now on" (ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν).

Stephen's vision as he was being stoned: "I see heaven opened and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God" ([ref:Acts 7:55-56|Acts 7:55-56]). This is a fulfillment of Jesus' words in Luke 22:69, where the Son of Man is actually seen exalted at the right hand of God's power.

Paul writes that God "raised Christ from the dead and seated him at his right hand in the heavenly places, far above all rule and authority" ([ref:Eph 1:20-21|Ephesians 1:20-21]). The theme of Christ's exaltation at God's right hand is the same as Jesus' statement that the Son of Man will sit at the right hand of God's power.

Paul urges believers: "Set your minds on things that are above, where Christ is seated at the right hand of God" ([ref:Col 3:1|Colossians 3:1]). Christ's position at God's right hand is a consistent confession in the early church and is a direct fulfillment of Jesus' words in Luke 22:69.

The letter to the Hebrews confesses that the Son "sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high" ([ref:Heb 1:3|Hebrews 1:3]). The expression "right hand of the Majesty" corresponds with "the right hand of God's power" (ἐκ δεξιῶν τῆς δυνάμεως τοῦ θεοῦ) in Luke 22:69.

"We have such a high priest who has sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in heaven" ([ref:Heb 8:1|Hebrews 8:1]). Once again, Christ's exalted position at God's right hand is confirmed, in line with Jesus' prophetic words during the trial.
